precepts.text: As for the ungodly, wrath came upon them without mercy unto the end: for he knew before what they would do. The chapter before goes into the destruction of Egypt, all the plagues that came. But here is what is very telling: he did not show mercy in his wrath, because he already knew what they were going to do.
precepts.point: It is like a director, a screenplay writer. They write the movie, and you show up as the actor. They give you the script and you read it and say, this is a good movie, who am I going to play? Oh, I am going to be the Black Panther. Somebody may be morally torn by playing Killmonger, but Killmonger is actually the good guy. My point is Michael B. Jordan agreed to that role. Chadwick Boseman agreed to that role. Everybody agreed to their role, and then the movie was made and we all watched it and we were cheering, Wakanda forever. The same way, the Lord sat in his council and everyone was given their roles, their tasks. He already knew who was who, who was ordained to be in this womb.

note.label: Stay in the Spirit

precepts.why:
Ezra says, “And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me. For then every one obeyed.” Before the world was made there was a council, and no one spoke against what was ordained. Christ said, these spirits over here, y’all are the twelve tribes of Israel; those spirits right there, y’all are the Jebusites. No one disagreed. When you are before the creator you are not going to say, no, I don’t want to be the Edomites.

It is like a screenplay writer and a director. You show up as the actor, they give you the script, and you say, this is a good movie, who am I going to play? Michael B. Jordan agreed to play Killmonger; they portrayed him as the bad guy, but Killmonger is actually the good guy. Chadwick Boseman agreed to his role. Everybody agreed to their role, then the movie was made and we cheered, Wakanda forever. The same way the Lord sat in his council and everyone was given their roles and tasks.

Wisdom of Solomon proves he knew beforehand: “As for the ungodly, wrath came upon them without mercy unto the end: for he knew before what they would do.” The chapter before goes into the destruction of Egypt and all the plagues that came. What is very telling is that he did not show mercy in his wrath, because he already knew what they were going to do.

So what Paul said and Peter said, the prophet Ezra says the same: it was ordained before the world was made. Now “the manners of them which are created in this world that is made are corrupted by a perpetual seed”, and the Lord already knew who would be ungodly and dealt with them accordingly.

precepts.text: For such as in their life have received benefits: that's the riches, the fame, the fortune. And they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty, when brothers on the street preaching and teaching, and when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it: the same must know it after death by pain.
precepts.point: That verse speaks volumes. Deceivableness: the easy word is deceit. Unrighteousness: sin. All deceit of sin, breaking God's laws. In them that perish, because they received not the love of the truth: this is about our people.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
“For such as in their life have received benefits, and have not known me”: that's the riches, the fame, the fortune. “And they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty”: while the brothers were on the street preaching and teaching.

“and, when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it; The same must know it after death by pain.” The door of repentance was open to them, and they despised it.

That is the end of them that perish in 2 Thessalonians 2:10. They received not the love of the truth, God's law, while they had time and liberty, and the same must know it after death by pain.

precepts.text: Then shall they be in pitiful case, which now have abused my ways, and they that have cast them away despitefully shall dwell in torments. For such as in their life have received benefits, and have not known me, and they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty, and when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it; the same must know it after death by pain. Discussed in class: a commentator who said he is not oppressed because he makes ten million dollars a year; that is a benefit received while not knowing God. He once posted Revelation 3:9 with no commentary, got attacked for it, and quickly deleted it. Who says when you die you don't get punished? Nobody escapes.
precepts.point: For it is not a light thing to do wickedly against the laws of God. Sometimes we take the laws of the Most High for granted with the mentality, I can sin and God won't do nothing.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

precepts.why:
“For it is not a light thing to do wickedly against the laws of God.” Sometimes we take God’s laws for granted with the mentality, I can sin and God won’t do nothing. Ezra shows otherwise: “Then shall they be in pitiful case, which now have abused my ways: and they that have cast them away despitefully shall dwell in torments.”

“For such as in their life have received benefits, and have not known me.” Look at Jason Whitlock. In the interview he said he is not oppressed because he makes ten million dollars a year. That is a benefit. A lot of our people become doctors and make big money and say, if I can do it, you can do it, and they do not know God. Whitlock once posted Revelation 3:9 on his Instagram with no commentary, all Amalek attacked him, and he quickly deleted it. These people need a wake-up call.

“And they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it.” They had liberty, because the brothers are out there teaching and the videos are in their feed. They see it, and they hate it.

“The same must know it after death by pain.” So who says that when you die you don’t get punished? You are going to know pain after you die, when Christ returns. Nobody escapes. That is why it is not a light thing to do wickedly against the laws of God, as Jason did.

precepts.text: Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee. Where did he know us? In the spirit, before our parents brought us forth. There is something in your spirit that God said, I need to fix you, so that when the time comes you come back to me and not to your pride.
precepts.point: The same must know it after death by pain. This is a God that will kill you and still have pain awaiting. So do not let anybody tell you the place of torment was made up by a church; these scriptures are in the book.

note.label: The Pride Of Thine Heart Hath Deceived Thee!

precepts.why:
Ezra says every one that shall be saved, and shall escape by his works, by keeping the commandments, and by faith in what is written, “Shall be preserved from the said perils, and shall see my salvation in my land, and within my borders: for I have sanctified them for me from the beginning.” That is when the kingdom is set up. And why does he say he sanctified them from the beginning? Jeremiah shows it.

“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee.” Where did he know us? In spirit. This is a physical domain, but he knew us in the spirit world, in another dimension. He did something to our spirit before our parents had relations to bring us forth. You are here because of a conversation God had with you before you even came into this world.

So you people are here because God cares about you. You are not here by accident. There is something in your spirit that God said, I need to fix you, so that when the time comes to destroy the earth, you come back to me and are not in your pride.

The third of Israelites were sanctified from the beginning, from the foundation of the earth. He said, these spirits I am going to love, and these spirits I am going to reject and destroy. God is good all the time to the people that keep his commandments. To you people breaking God’s laws, he is not good. So do not listen to anybody saying God is good all the time; that is not scriptural.

That is why the rest of the chapter is so hard: those who abused his ways, loathed his law while they had liberty and despised the place of repentance “must know it after death by pain.” The sanctified are preserved; the proud are not.

precepts.text: Let the multitude perish which was born in vain: the nations are the extras in the movie, and we are the stars.
precepts.point: Fear thou not, O my servant Jacob: what he says will happen makes us afraid, so we increase our faith by remembering this body is a shell. I will save thee from afar and thy seed from the land of their captivity, and Jacob shall return and be in rest and none shall make him afraid. Though I make a full end of all nations, the extras born in vain with Esau the villain, I will not make a full end of thee, but correct thee in measure and not leave thee altogether unpunished.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
“though I make a full end of all nations whither I have scattered thee, yet will I not make a full end of thee”. Why is he going to make an end of all nations? Ezra says it: “Let the multitude perish then, which was born in vain”.

All these nations were born in vain. In a movie they are the extras; they're not the stars of the movie. We are. And Esau is the villain, the antagonist, the bad guy.

But the stars are not spared from correction: “I will correct thee in measure, and will not leave thee altogether unpunished.” The Lord makes a full end of the nations, but only corrects Israel in measure. So “fear thou not, O my servant Jacob”. What he says will happen would make anyone afraid, and nobody wants to go through tribulation, so we increase our faith by reminding ourselves that this body is just a shell; the real us is within. He will save us from afar, and Jacob shall return and be in rest, and none shall make him afraid.

precepts.text: Everyone that shall be saved and escape by his works and by faith whereby ye have believed: works and faith, not one without the other.
precepts.point: Abraham was justified by works when he offered Isaac; faith wrought with his works and by works was faith made perfect, and he was called the friend of God. By works a man is justified and not by faith only, as Romans 2:13 said, and Rahab was justified by works when she sent the spies out another way. As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

precepts.why:
“Even so faith, if it hath not works, is dead, being alone.” People say the law can’t save you, you are not justified by the works of the law. Ezra answers it: “And every one that shall be saved, and shall be able to escape by his works, and by faith, whereby ye have believed.”

Everyone that shall be saved shall escape by what? His works. And by faith. Works and faith go hand in hand; you have to have both, as James said. You will be saved by both: not faith alone and no works, not faith and no commandments, not commandments and no faith. That makes no sense; it is dead, being alone.

“though a man say he hath faith, and have not works? can faith save him?” That is like a man saying I got a paycheck, with no job. I get paid tomorrow. You got a job? No. It is the dumbest thing you can say out of your mouth. Your faith proves your works and your works prove your faith. Abraham had faith and kept the commandments of God, and his keeping the commandments proved his faith.

And it goes back to the royal law, loving your neighbour as yourself. Telling a brother with no food and no clothes “be ye warmed and filled”, and giving him nothing, makes no damn sense. Even so, faith without works makes no sense: the faith does not exist.

precepts.text: Whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.
precepts.point: The angel who spoke to John called himself his fellow servant and his brother.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Ezra hears the Lord say, “when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me.” Before the earth was made, his children were with him and they obeyed. Revelation shows that the choosing was done back then: “all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.”

From where? From the foundation of the world. When was your name written in the book of life? At the foundation of the world. That goes back to Genesis 1, when the Lord divided the light from the darkness and separated good from evil. That is predestination.

There is no heathen in that book. I don't care how good you think he is; they are not in the book of life. They are in the book of slavery, the register of chains. Those whose names are not written there worship the beast, because they were not chosen from the foundation of the world. And those who were written there are the ones who, in the beginning, before the world was made, did not speak against him.

precepts.text: I am thy fellow servant, and of thy brethren the prophets.
precepts.point: The angel who spoke to John called himself his fellow servant and his brother.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
When the world was not yet made, “no man spake against me”: everyone obeyed. We were there with the Lord in the beginning in our angelic bodies, not in this wicked fleshly body. To see what that means, look at the angel who spoke to John.

John fell down to worship before the feet of the angel, and the angel said, “See thou do it not: for I am thy fellowservant, and of thy brethren the prophets, and of them which keep the sayings of this book: worship God.” I am a servant just like you. I am your brother. I am a prophet. And I am of them which keep the sayings of this book. That is heavy.

So now you understand a little more what the Lord means when he says that when we were with him in the beginning, we all obeyed. The angels are our brethren; we had that same celestial body with him before the earth was created, and that is why Christ says those who understand the power of God will be equal unto the angels. Now, covered in this flesh, we are rebellious, and the Lord has to keep whooping us for our idols and our evil. But you have to see who you are and believe it. This is not a fairy tale; this is real.

precepts.text: We have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.
precepts.point: The angel who spoke to John called himself his fellow servant and his brother.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
Before the world was made, everyone obeyed, because we were not in the flesh. Paul shows the body we had and will have again: “For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.” If this body is dissolved, we have a body, not made with hands like Adam formed of the dust of the ground, but eternal in the heavens: a celestial body.

“For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven”. We groan in this body because it is susceptible to sin, and we want our body from heaven. “If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.” That is what Adam's nakedness was: not running around naked, but being in the flesh. Before, he had a spiritual body; God took his spirit and put it in the flesh. That nakedness is the shame, the sinful nature.

We groan “not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life.” We want our immortal body. “we walk by faith, not by sight”, “willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord.”

So when you die keeping the commandments, you are present with the Lord. This is for every brother and sister who is sick, who has been told they do not have long to live, and for those who have passed away: we understand where they are. Don't be afraid. Conquer that fear. If you did what was right on this earth and dealt right with the saints, absent from this body, you will be with the Lord.

precepts.point: The glory the Father gave him he has given us, because we had it before; and where he is now is where his children will be when paradise comes down here.

precepts.text: The law perisheth not but remaineth in his force; the dietary law did not change.
precepts.point: The law perisheth not, but remaineth in his force; that law did not change at all. Do not let anybody confuse you, especially if you are new in the truth: eat what the Most High instructed you to eat.

note.label: Leviticus 11: The Dietary Law of Clean and Unclean Beasts

precepts.why:
“Notwithstanding the law perisheth not, but remaineth in his force.” The dietary law did not change at all. “ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy” is still the word, and the way to be holy in what you eat is still the law of the beasts.

Do not let anybody confuse you, especially if you are new in the truth. The law of the beast and of the fowl and of every living creature remains in force: eat what the Most High instructed you to eat, and make the difference between the unclean and the clean.

precepts.text: Those who abused God's ways and cast his words away shall dwell in torment; having had liberty and despised repentance, they shall know it after death by pain.
precepts.point: Christ sat with sinners, but he was correcting them and showing them righteousness, not indulging their sin. We go to the streets to talk with sinners and give them the scriptures the same way.

note.label: Psalm 7: David's Prayer for Deliverance in the Last Days

precepts.why:
Ezra shows what happens when the space for repentance is over. “Then shall they be in pitiful case, which now have abused my ways: and they that have cast them away despitefully shall dwell in torments. For such as in their life have received benefits, and have not known me; And they that have loathed my law, while they had yet liberty, and, when as yet place of repentance was open unto them, understood not, but despised it; The same must know it after death by pain.”

Those who abused God's ways and cast his words away shall dwell in torment. They had liberty and a place of repentance open to them, and they despised it; so they must know it after death by pain.

That is the end of the wicked God is angry with every day. The mercy of Christ holds back his fury now and keeps the place of repentance open. Those who use that time to repent are judged as the righteous; those who loathe his law while they have liberty know it after death.

precepts.text: Hear O Israel, I sow My law in you and it shall bring forth fruit; the law has to be sown in our minds, which is why we are told to study, pray, and apply.
precepts.point: Rejoice in the Lord ye righteous, and give thanks at the remembrance of His holiness. He did not forget us; He chastened us for a little but He did not forget, and He is going to remember the covenant.

note.label: Psalm 97: A Fire Goeth Before Him

precepts.why:
Light is sown for the righteous, and the Most High says himself what he sows. “Hear me, O Israel; and mark my words, thou seed of Jacob. For, behold, I sow my law in you, and it shall bring fruit in you, and ye shall be honoured in it for ever.”

The law has to be sown in our minds, and that is why we are told to study, pray and apply. Sown that way, it brings forth fruit in us: the fruits of repentance, loving the Lord and loving our neighbour. That is the gladness of the upright in heart, and we give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness because he did not forget us. He chastened us for a little, but he did not forget, and he is going to remember the covenant.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why: What are the works? Revelation 14:12 tells you it is faith and works: “Here is the patience of the saints: here are they that keep the commandments of God, and the faith of Jesus.” The works are keeping the commandments, and the faith is faith in Christ. That is how everyone that shall be saved shall escape.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why: What does “I have sanctified them for me from the beginning” mean? “God hath from the beginning chosen you to salvation”: he has chosen us from the beginning, talking about Genesis, “through sanctification of the Spirit and belief of the truth.”

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
“And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me.” In the beginning, before the earth was made, no man spake against him. “For then every one obeyed”: we were all there with him in the beginning, and then everyone obeyed.

“But now the manners of them which are created in this world that is made are corrupted by a perpetual seed, and by a law which is unsearchable rid themselves.” So the ones he sanctified from the beginning are the ones that were with him before the world was made.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
“And now when I prepared the world, which was not yet made, even for them to dwell in that now live, no man spake against me.” In the beginning, before the earth was made, no man spake against him. “For then every one obeyed”: we were all there with him in the beginning, and then everyone obeyed.

“But now the manners of them which are created in this world that is made are corrupted by a perpetual seed, and by a law which is unsearchable rid themselves.” So the ones he sanctified from the beginning are the ones that were with him before the world was made.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
“With all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish”: them that perish are our people, “because they received not the love of the truth”, which is faith in Christ and keeping the commandments, “that they might be saved.”

“And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: That they all might be damned.” What is that word? Damned. That is the same thing Christ said in Matthew 23:33. “Who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness”: that is them, these pastors. Their damnation is the torments of 2 Esdras 9:9.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
Keys of hell and death. Christ is speaking: “I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death.” Wait a minute: Christ says he has the keys of hell and death.

Hell in the context of the grave is the sentence on all flesh; everybody dies, so this is not talking about that. Sorrow, trouble, oppression and slavery have been going on from the beginning, so it is not talking about that either. This hell, this death, is the damnation we read about in Matthew 23. It is not a car crash. This death and hell is the torment; it is what they shall know “after death by pain.”

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why: Back to it one more time: “Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?” The damnation of hell. Christ is not talking about the grave, which is the sentence on all flesh. He is not talking about sorrow, captivity or trouble in the flesh. This is that torment, which many of our people don’t believe in.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why: “What I tell you in darkness”: what I told you in private, “that speak ye in light”: I want you to speak it openly before all the people. “And what ye hear in the ear”: what I’ve told you in your ear privately, “that preach ye upon the housetops”: go on the housetops and preach it loud to everybody. What he told us in parables, he wants us to make plain to the people. But in the same token he’s saying, what you going to say out there is going to get you killed.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
“And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul”: he says that because what we preach in public will get us killed. “But rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.” In where? In hell. That’s the damnation.

Man can only kill the flesh, this body. Once this is gone your soul is still alive; the real you is alive. But Christ said, if you disobey, fear the Lord, that can kill not just your body but your soul too, in hell. That’s damnation, the pain after death.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why: “Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father.” A bird does not die without the Father’s consent, and he’s talking about us. “But the very hairs of your head are all numbered”: that’s how important you are, you Israelites; every hair on our head is numbered. “Fear ye not therefore, ye are of more value than many sparrows”: you’re more important than birds, brothers and sisters.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
Go back to verse 28, fear not them which kill the body, then 32: “Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men”, that’s in fear of death, “him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.” If you ain’t afraid, he’s going to confess you before the heavenly Father.

“But whosoever shall deny me before men”, because you scared to die. You don’t want this flesh burned, your head cut off, to be stabbed, dragged behind a car, whiplashed, or tied by your arms and legs to horses and ripped apart. Christ said, “him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.” And guess what that is: damnation. Christ denying you is damnation.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
“But he that sinneth against me wrongeth his own soul.” All you adulterers out there, listen good: you ain’t wronging us, you are wronging your own soul. He didn’t say you wrong your own body; he said you wrong your soul.

“All they that hate me love death.” What kind of death is that talking about? It ain’t talking about the death of your body, because he is talking about your soul. This is that damnation.
